title: The Savoy years and Charlie Buchanan
summary: From 1955 to 1962 he led seven pieces at the Savoy, hired by manager Charlie Buchanan, who kept him because he played all the dance nights.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: not anything comes to your mind, anything particularly significant, during those years when you had the big band, well then, in, let's see, we said '42 to '55, I think you had the big band. And then from '55 to '62, you had the seven pieces at the Savoy. Did you go out at all from there, with the seven pieces?
Very seldom.
Yeah. You were mostly there.
Yeah.
And was that in any way due to Charlie Buchanan, the Savoy? Or was that strictly, as far as -- or simply that Moe Gale just hired you.
No, not Moe Gale. Charlie Buchanan. He was the manager.
The manager of your band?
No. The manager of the Savoy.
The manager of the Savoy, yeah. So you mean Charlie hired you.
Yeah.
Oh. Well, why was I always under the impression that the Savoy was physically or financially tied up with the Gale agency too? Were Charlie and Moe partners in some way?
Yeah.
Yeah. They weren't equal partners?
No. I think --
Well, Charlie probably started off in a small way, and got bigger.
Yeah. And got bigger, yeah.
Yeah. One --

But the main reason why they kept me there, Helen, not because I was Cootie Williams, a jazz player. It was because I produced. They used to have certain nights for certain types of music. And I learned to play that type of music. They used to have on Wednesday nights, club nights, where they would have the older people there. And I learned how to play the waltzes and the slow music. On Monday nights and Thursday nights, that was jitterbug night. I had to learn to play their type of music. So they wanted me, the jitterbugs. And the older crowd that come there, they wanted me. And on Sunday afternoon, they would have matinees, club dances, and I used to learn how to play club music for that type of thing. So I was well rounded, with all types of music to play for the types of people that came to the Savoy Ballroom.
Yeah. Yeah.
So that's the main reason why Charlie Buchanan kept me there.
Yeah. Yeah. Because you filled the bill.
Yeah.
Everybody's bill. Yeah. I see. Well,
you wouldn't -- you didn't have too much trouble with the guys, then, because you were on location. I mean, everybody likes to stay in town.
Yeah. Everybody likes to stay in town.
